_about: Game tuning values. Unless a 'basis' says otherwise these are invented starting values for balancing (see docs/planning/04_game_design.md section 8.5).

pace.basis: Pace calibrated so normal averages about 6.2 mi/day with rests: Uys party, Grahamstown to Sand River, Apr-29 Jun 1837 (05_research_pass2.md section 2); about 10 km/day with herds (02 section 3).

oxen.basis: Harris (1836) lost many oxen on a fast march; rates invented.

night_risk.basis: invented; Vegkop (1836) shows a laager's protective effect

mend.basis: invented. A day's mending on the road: each worn part gains gain + gain_per_smith x the best smith's skill (more for the smith family), using iron_lb of bar iron (half without), up to cap; a part below spare_below is replaced by a spare if one is carried; tallow greases wheels and axle; the tent is patched up to tent_cap, or new canvas makes it whole. Trekkers tightened tyres, greased axles and patched tents at outspans [recall, verify].

smith_basis: estimate: a town smith charges this many pence per point of wear put right, times the town's price_mul; putting a broken wheel right costs a little under a new spare wheel (240d).

illness_per_day.basis: invented; tuned with trekbot so a careful Normal run loses about one person in five trips, near the child mortality of the period (about 160-200 per 1,000 births a year, Mamre 1837-46; 05 section 6)

servant_wage.basis: 10 Rds / 15s a month: Steedman (c. 1832), Backhouse (1838). Paid in sheep (about 3 Rds each, Steedman) when there is no cash: invented rule; paying servants in livestock is [recall, verify].
